assessments.reasoning: Both HTTP 200 receipts from oss.oracle.com match the bound range and full-response digests and cover [0,18435) contiguously. In half-open byte offsets, the agreement text occupies [0,17901), from “COMMON DEVELOPMENT AND DISTRIBUTION LICENSE (CDDL) Version 1.1” through the final period of Section 10’s “shall be deemed to constitute any admission of liability.” Two LF bytes precede the separator at [17903,17975), and two more precede the notice at byte 17977. The heading reads “NOTICE PURSUANT TO SECTION 9 OF THE COMMON DEVELOPMENT AND DISTRIBUTION LICENSE (CDDL)” across two lines. It specifies California law excluding conflict-of-law provisions, jurisdiction of the Federal Courts of the Northern District of California and the state courts of the State of California, and venue in Santa Clara County, California. Its final period ends the text at byte boundary 18433, followed by two LF bytes.

Both HTTP 200 receipts for the SPDX repository’s commit-qualified text/CDDL-1.1.txt match the bound range and full-response digests and cover [0,17390) contiguously. SPDX places “Version 1.1” on its own line, uses typographic quotation marks, changes wrapping and indentation, and places the same notice after Section 10 without the hyphen rule. The JavaScript comparison preserved the wording and order of the agreement and notice and detected the changed Section 2 heading.

The complete 700-byte HTTP 200 GitHub Git objects API response matches the bound SHA-256. It identifies annotated object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0 in spdx/license-list-data and gives its target type as commit and target SHA as 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This establishes release provenance for the acquired text. The API explicitly reports the tag as unsigned.

limitations: The crosswalk covers only these two pinned representations of CDDL-1.1. Their bytes differ. Other editions and releases fall outside the comparison.

Section 9 refers to a notice contained within the Original Software. The attached California notice applies by its own terms. Its inclusion in both representations establishes no license or venue determination for an unrelated project.

The finding is descriptive and limited to edition identity, text correspondence, and release provenance. Approval classification, canonical admission, redistribution, and publication decisions are outside its scope.
The annotated tag is unsigned. Its release-to-commit mapping is evidenced by the pinned GitHub API response.
